statement: The reported diagonal grade second-variation cross-term X_{zeta,diag}(a, v) = (log tau)^2 [(a^2 - v)S_2(a) - a S_1(a)] has an exact cancellation variance v_*(a) = a^2 - a S_1(a)/S_2(a) such that X_{zeta,diag}(a, v_*(a)) = 0 identically. Because S_2(a) >= (log 2) S_1(a) > 0 for all a > 0, the cancellation variance v_*(a) is strictly positive for all a > 1/log 2. Universal non-vanishing over all a > 0, v >= 0 is false and withdrawn.
hypotheses: S_1(a) = sum_{n>=2} Lambda(n)^2 n^{-1-2a} log n > 0
object_studied: Reported diagonal fragment of the grade-dilated Dirichlet polynomial second variation cross-term
fourier_normalization: Centered coordinates z = s - 1/2 = a + it; tau = 2pi; Fourier transform hat{W}(xi) = int W(t) e^{-it xi} dt
measure_and_window: Centered normalized probability window W in C_c^infty(R) with variance v = int t^2 W(t) dt
order_of_limits: Evaluation for fixed positive integer truncation max_n and infinite limit a > 1/2
exact_conclusion: (a^2 - v_*(a)) S_2(a) - a S_1(a) = 0 and v_*(a) > 0 for all a > 1/log 2; X_{zeta,diag} changes sign across v_*(a)
logical_negation: For all a > 0 and all v >= 0, (a^2 - v) S_2(a) - a S_1(a) != 0 (FALSIFIED by witness (a, v_*(a)))
falsification_attempts: Constructed exact algebraic root and equality case cancellation analysis v_*(a) = a^2 - a S_1/S_2
Proved S_2/S_1 >= log 2 > 0 for all a > 0
Evaluated boundary asymptotic dominance: quadratic a^2 strictly dominates linear -a as a -> infinity
Proved positive variance realizability via smooth dilation W_lambda(t) = (1/lambda) W_0(t/lambda)
Separated diagonal fragment from complete finite-window off-diagonal terms
